name: OpenCPN
description: CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER=0 explicitly set (with a FIXME) disabling TLS for the plugin catalog + native-plugin tarball downloads; SHA-256 fails open and comes from the same unverified catalog. [Opus-verified: CONFIRMED-D]
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: The plugin downloader disables TLS verification, accepts an empty catalog checksum, and passes the archive into native-plugin installation. This supports the plugin channel; primary app update scope is unresolved.
limitations: Source review is limited to the retained commit and does not establish released-artifact or current-upstream behavior.

original_evidence.text: | OpenCPN | https://github.com/OpenCPN/OpenCPN | 01873e3 / 2026-08-19 | **Y** (native plugin manager) | N (manual, via Plugin Manager UI; not run at startup) | **Y** | **HTTPS URL, but TLS cert validation explicitly DISABLED in code** | N | SHA-256 hash, but **fail-open + hash sourced from the same unauthenticated channel** | none (hash delivered via same untrusted catalog fetch) | **`model/src/downloader.cpp:78`** and **`:124`**: `curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER, 0L);` (preceded by `// FIXME -- Add correct certificates on host.`) in the shared `Downloader` class used for BOTH the plugin catalog fetch (`model/src/catalog_handler.cpp:116-130`, `DOWNLOAD_REPO="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCPN/plugins"`) and the plugin tarball download (`gui/src/download_mgr.cpp:115-165`, `GuiDownloader` extends `Downloader`); `gui/src/download_mgr.cpp:67-98` `checksum_ok()` computes SHA-256 of the downloaded tarball and compares to `metadata.checksum` — but that checksum comes from the very same TLS-unverified catalog fetch, AND if `metadata.checksum == ""` the function returns `true` (`download_mgr.cpp:70-72`, fail-open, no check at all); `model/src/plugin_handler.cpp:1209-1238` `InstallPlugin()` then extracts the tarball and loads it as a native plugin. Net effect: any on-path attacker (no CA-trusted cert needed) can MITM both the catalog and the tarball and supply a matching forged checksum — full RCE, worse than typical CDN-compromise since TLS itself is defeated |
